description: Post-Lousetown chalcedonic sinter: white to gray, largely low in porosity, chalcedonized; opaline sinter still porous and fragmental in places; relict bedding nearly horizontal, gravity-controlled chalcedony fillings
notes: sinter treated as part of the Qal (surface deposits) unit

description: Pre-Lake Lahontan alluvium: silt, sand and fine gravel, some pebbles to 20 mm; acid altered near top, white to cream, gray below; Steamboat basaltic andesite abundant in basal 12 ft
Steamboat basaltic andesite of the Lousetown Formation: lava flow with scoriaceous aa top grading to massive lava below 98 ft; zone dipping 45-60 deg near 109 ft, probably a fault with clastic dike
Pre-Lousetown alluvium: silt, sand and abundant gravel (to 3 in.), fragments largely granitic and soda trachyte, no apparent bedding
Alta Formation: felsitic lava (soda trachyte relicts), completely altered but hard; basal foot or more argillized fine-grained tuff
Silt, sand and fine gravel, angular, white, consisting entirely of granitic debris; hydrothermally altered to illite-montmorillonite, chalcedony, potassium feldspar
notes: printed under the Alta Formation heading in the log; treated as alluvium because it is granitic debris

description: Granodiorite: 'rotten' near top with thoroughly argillized plagioclase and hornblende but generally some nearly fresh biotite; kaolinite near top, illite-montmorillonite in middle, potassium feldspar near bottom; rare aplite dikes with little or no hydrothermal effects
notes: altered granodiorite by the project's classify_formation_unit rule; White's log ends at 210 ft, the hole total depth is 212 ft (White 1968 Table 32, NBMG), and the last 2 ft are not described
